profile.headline: Full-Stack Web Developer
profile.summary:
Hi! I’m Amanda. I help businesses and entrepreneurs turn ideas into reliable, scalable web applications. Whether you need a new site built from the ground up or improvements to an existing web application, I focus on building custom systems that meet your business goals.

While Rails is my specialty, I’m comfortable switching to whatever your project needs: React, WordPress, Django, or beyond. Clients appreciate my clear communication, collaborative approach, and ability to translate technical details into results. With a background in teaching and award-winning tutoring, I know how to break down problems, adapt quickly, and deliver solutions that work.

If you’re looking for a developer who will treat your project like their own and focus on results, let’s talk.

positions.title: Founder & Principal Software Engineer
positions.description:
Zoa Systems is how I take on independent software development work for small and mid-sized businesses. Whether you're starting from scratch or evolving an existing system, I handle the full lifecycle: from wireframes and prototypes through MVP, production deployment, and ongoing DevOps.

What I work on:
- Full-stack web application development (greenfield and legacy migrations)
- E-commerce platforms and payment integrations
- Custom business tooling: inventory management, order management, internal dashboards, and data workflows
- Feature development and enhancements on existing codebases
- Site administration, hosting, and infrastructure management

How I engage:
I work directly with founders, operators, and technical leads: no account managers, no handoffs. You get a single point of contact who understands both the business problem and the technical solution, from the first conversation to final delivery.

positions.title: Lead Developer & Associate Chicken Farmer
positions.description:
Henventory is my first-ever web app: a full-stack Ruby on Rails 8 application that helps chicken farmers track egg production, built with PostgreSQL, Tailwind CSS, and Stimulus.js. My technical mentor gave me the tools and support I needed to make this project a success.

Deployed to production in March 2025 on Render, and it's still actively maintained with bug fixes & performance optimization. New features are currently in development~

While building this app, I've been responsible for the part-time care of 11 chickens. It's a great way to get away from the machine to relax, and to let your subconscious sort through problems with your code. Watching chickens run is great for laughs, too. It's one of the funniest things I've ever seen.

Technical highlights:
- Multi-user household system with invite tokens and shared data access
- Dual tracking modes (per-chicken and flock-wide) with domain-specific validation (max 1 egg per chicken per day)
- Calendar-based pagination and timezone-aware data entry with Flatpickr - N+1 query optimization and memory profiling after a production memory crisis (97% down to 35%)
- Rails 8 authentication with rate-limited login and session management
- Test suite with model, controller, and system tests

This is how I learned Rails. Things got messy, but I learned a lot about Active Record, database design, deployment, debugging, and stress management. I even managed to cut down my caffeine consumption during the process.

Key Technologies: Ruby on Rails 8, PostgreSQL, Hotwire (Turbo/Stimulus), Tailwind CSS, Render, Solid Queue, Pagy

positions.title: Full Stack Developer
positions.description:
A production e-commerce platform built with Ruby on Rails 8, PostgreSQL, & Stripe, for a small business in the botanical wellness space.

Led end-to-end development of this greenfield e-comm platform for the company's US market expansion, owning every phase from requirements gathering & wireframing through architecture, implementation, & deployment.

Designed database schema, service layer, & payment pipeline using Rails 8, PostgreSQL, & Stripe, with focus on data integrity, payment idempotency, & webhook security.

Built the full UI/UX using Turbo/Stimulus & Tailwind CSS.

Currently preparing for production launch on Render.

Architecture Highlights:
- Service layer with five modular service objects following SRP and .call conventions: cart management, payment handling, webhook sync, admin fulfillment, & Stripe caching
- Dual-path payment processing: synchronous controller path and asynchronous webhook path coordinated via pessimistic database locking to prevent race conditions & guarantee idempotent payment handling, regardless of which path fires first
- Webhook sig verification for Stripe (HMAC) & Cloudinary (SHA1), with Redis-backed duplicate event detection to prevent replay attacks
- Reusable SoftDeletable concern with cascading soft-deletes across associations, preserving audit trails while keeping active queries clean
- Webhook-drive cache invalidation: Stripe product/price changes & Cloudinary uploads invalidate Redis caches on-demand rather than relying on polling
- Background job pipeline via Solid Queue for async payment retry with exponential backoff, abandoned cart cleanup, & Algolia search index sync
- Session-based anonymous shopping cart with uniqueness constraints scoped to soft-deletion state
- Rails 8 native auth: rate-limited login, signed HTTP-only cookies, and admin-scoped session management

Stack: Rails 8, PostgreSQL, Stripe (Embedded Checkout, Products API, Webhooks), Redis, Solid Queue, Turbo/Stimulus, Tailwind CSS v4, Cloudinary, Algolia
